title: W002 initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke
description:
W002 workset epic: Initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke.

Goal: drive the first executable OxForms slice from plan to evidence. This workset proves the architecture direction by having VBA-authored smoke code emit a minimal FillRect display-list command, a Rust PAL receive and render it headlessly with stable diagnostics, and a Windows visible smoke path paint the same command.

Read first:
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md, especially Purpose, Non-goals, Architecture Slice, Closure Condition, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, 9, 10.2, and the W002 bootstrap slice in section 11.
- docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md section OxVba Development Baseline for pinned dependency policy.

Non-goals for the whole epic: do not implement full UserForm.Show, .frm/.frx parsing, intrinsic controls, text metrics, input routing, timers, clipboard, image decode, or MSForms parity claims. The smoke API is allowed to be temporary and must be named/treated as smoke-only.
design:
Execution model:
1. oxforms-dwm.1 finishes the self-contained bead/workset plan.
2. oxforms-dwm.2 scaffolds the Rust/VBA workspace using the pinned OxVba dependency policy.
3. oxforms-dwm.3 implements DisplayList/FillRect and a deterministic headless renderer.
4. oxforms-dwm.4 proves VBA -> OxVba -> PAL with the same rectangle command.
5. oxforms-dwm.5 adds a Windows visible smoke path from the same display list.
6. oxforms-dwm.6 records evidence, reviews the whole workset, updates docs, and closes the workset when objective checks pass.

The graph is intentionally mostly linear until the display-list core exists; then VBA and Windows smoke can proceed from the same renderer contract. Headless rendering is the automated oracle; visible Windows rendering is important but should not become a flaky CI gate.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic is complete only when:
- oxforms-dwm.2 through oxforms-dwm.6 are closed with their acceptance checks satisfied.
- The Rust PAL renders a FillRect display list headlessly with stable checked diagnostics/hash.
- The OxVba-driven VBA smoke emits/submits the same rectangle command and reaches the PAL seam.
- The Windows visible smoke exists and is verified on Windows, or a concrete blocker/follow-up bead records why it could not be verified.
- Evidence records commands, artifacts, hashes, platform notes, and fresh-eyes review outcome.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md and docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md accurately describe final status.
notes:
Dependency: W002 depends on oxforms-rzk / W001 repo bootstrap. Do not start implementation beads until W001 and oxforms-dwm.1 are closed.

Review rule for every child bead: At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.

title: Scaffold OxForms Rust/VBA workspace for PAL smoke
description:

- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, and 9.

Scope:
- Create the smallest Rust workspace layout needed for W002, expected to include a root Cargo.toml and an oxforms-pal crate or equivalent local crate name matching the workset language.
- Add discoverable locations for VBA smoke sources/fixtures, but do not implement the full smoke behavior yet.
- Encode the pinned OxVba dependency policy from docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md. Do not commit a dependency on a floating ../OxVba sibling checkout. If local path overrides are useful for development, keep them out of committed shared manifests or document them as local-only.

design:

title: Implement display-list core and headless rectangle renderer
description:
Implementation bead: implement the display-list core and deterministic headless rectangle renderer.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Architecture Slice items 1-2, Closure Condition items 1 and 5, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.4 Display Lists, 6.2 Contract Surface, and 10.2 Fidelity Strategy.
- The workspace scaffold from oxforms-dwm.2.

Scope:
- Define the first stable-enough smoke display-list data model: version, logical surface dimensions, Rect, Color with explicit byte order, DisplayCommand::FillRect, and DisplayList.
- Implement validation for obviously invalid rectangles/surfaces where useful for deterministic behavior.
- Implement a deterministic headless renderer that fills an in-memory buffer and returns RenderDiagnostics containing at least dimensions, command count, and a stable hash/checksum.
- Add focused tests that render a known small rectangle fixture and assert the diagnostic/hash. Prefer tests that are deterministic across Windows/non-Windows hosts.
- Add or update docs/evidence or a fixture manifest only if there is a real artifact to preserve at this stage.

Non-goals:
- No VBA/OxVba execution in this bead.
- No visible Windows window in this bead.
- No text, images, input, timers, system colors, or MSForms themed controls.
design:
Design notes:
- Keep W002 to FillRect only. Resist adding line/ellipse/text/image commands until a later bead/workset needs them.
- Use headless rendering as the automated oracle. The later Windows smoke must consume the same DisplayList rather than defining a parallel command path.
- If serialization is added, version it. If serialization is deferred, ensure the in-memory contract is still explicit enough for oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5 to share.
- Choose a hash/checksum that is stable and easy to recompute in tests; do not use nondeterministic timing or platform paint output as the core oracle.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Rust tests prove a known FillRect display list renders to the expected deterministic diagnostics/hash.
- The display-list and renderer API are documented enough in code/tests for oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5 to use without reinterpreting the plan.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace pass, unless a check is not yet applicable and the reason is documented with a follow-up bead.
- git diff --check, br dep cycles, and br ready --json pass.
- Commit code, tests, docs/evidence if any, and bead state with this bead ID in the message.
notes:
Dependencies: blocked by oxforms-dwm.2. Blocks oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5.

At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.
close_reason: Implemented versioned FillRect display list and deterministic headless RGBA8 renderer with stable diagnostics/hash; required Rust, git diff, and bead graph checks pass.

title: Execute VBA rectangle smoke through OxVba and PAL host seam
description:
Implementation bead: execute the VBA rectangle smoke through OxVba and the OxForms PAL host seam.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Architecture Slice items 3-4, Closure Condition item 2, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md section OxVba Development Baseline.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.2 VBA-first Implementation Contract, 4.4 Rendering Architecture, and 9 Runtime Integration with the OxVba VM.
- The DisplayList/headless renderer API and tests from oxforms-dwm.3.

Scope:
- Add a small VBA smoke source or fixture under the OxForms repo that constructs the same rectangle display list used by the Rust fixture.
- Add the minimum Rust/OxVba harness needed to execute that VBA smoke and route its FillRect command through the OxForms PAL seam into the headless renderer or a shared diagnostic path.
- Keep this as a procedural/class smoke. Do not require .frm ingestion or UserForm.Show; OxVba MODPROJ-030 is still forms-deferred unless docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md has been updated.
- Assert that the OxVba-driven path produces the same command/diagnostic/hash as the Rust fixture from oxforms-dwm.3.
- Add logging that makes failures understandable: which command was emitted, what diagnostics were expected, and what diagnostics were observed.

Non-goals:
- No visible Windows window; that belongs to oxforms-dwm.5.
- No full MSForms object model, Controls collection, events, or designer-declared members.
- No broad OxVba runtime changes unless absolutely required; if OxVba needs changes, create a handover or follow-up bead rather than editing sibling repos.
design:
Design notes:
- The smoke API may look like OxForms.CreateSmokeCanvas / FillRect / Flush, but it must be documented/named as smoke-only and not final compatibility API.
- Prefer a harness that reuses the headless renderer from oxforms-dwm.3 so the proof is against the same oracle.
- Use the pinned OxVba rev from docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md for committed dependencies. Local path overrides are development-only unless this bead deliberately updates the baseline doc.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- A documented command/test executes the VBA rectangle smoke through OxVba and reaches the PAL seam.
- The observed rectangle command/diagnostic/hash matches the Rust fixture from oxforms-dwm.3.
- Failure output is specific enough for a future agent to debug without re-reading this conversation.
- Applicable checks pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, targeted OxVba smoke command, git diff --check, br dep cycles, br ready --json.
- Docs/evidence are updated if the smoke command or artifact path becomes part of the workset truth.
- Commit code, tests, evidence/docs if any, and bead state with this bead ID in the message.

Dependencies: blocked by oxforms-dwm.3. Blocks oxforms-dwm.6.

title: Add Windows visible rectangle smoke backend
description:
Implementation bead: add the Windows visible rectangle smoke backend.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Architecture Slice item 5, Closure Condition item 3, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.1 Proposed Workspace Layout, 6.1 Backend Philosophy, 6.2 Contract Surface, and 10.1 Platforms.
- The DisplayList/headless renderer API from oxforms-dwm.3.

Scope:
- Add the smallest Windows-backed visible path that can paint the same FillRect DisplayList produced by the headless renderer tests.
- The visible smoke may be an example, ignored test, or manual command. It must be clearly documented and must not be the only verification path.
- On Windows, the smoke should open a small surface/window, paint the rectangle, and close deterministically or document the manual close step.
- On non-Windows hosts, the command/test should report an explicit unsupported diagnostic rather than failing mysteriously.
- Reuse the same DisplayList contract from oxforms-dwm.3. Do not invent a separate Windows-only command path.

Non-goals:
- No event loop breadth beyond what is needed to show the rectangle.
- No input routing, modal/modeless Show semantics, DPI fidelity, text, images, or controls.
- No replacement for the headless oracle.
design:
Design notes:
- Keep dependencies conservative. If choosing winit/tiny-skia/etc., document why in code or docs and keep the integration minimal.
- Avoid flaky automation. If a visible test cannot be deterministic in normal CI, mark it ignored/manual and leave headless renderer tests as the required gate.
- The value of this bead is plumbing confidence and developer-visible feedback, not pixel-perfect MSForms fidelity.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- A documented Windows-only smoke command/example/test paints the same rectangle display list as oxforms-dwm.3.
- Non-Windows behavior is an explicit unsupported/skip diagnostic.
- Headless tests still pass and remain the automated oracle.
- Applicable checks pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, any targeted ignored/manual smoke dry-run that is safe on the current host, git diff --check, br dep cycles, br ready --json.
- If Windows verification cannot be performed, create a concrete blocker/follow-up bead and record it before closing.
- Commit code, docs/evidence if any, and bead state with this bead ID in the message.
notes:
Dependencies: blocked by oxforms-dwm.3. Blocks oxforms-dwm.6. Priority is P2 because oxforms-dwm.4 is the critical VBA-first proof, but W002 cannot close without this bead or a concrete blocker/follow-up.

At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.

title: Record rectangle smoke evidence and fresh-eyes review
description:
Closure bead: record W002 rectangle smoke evidence, perform fresh-eyes review, and close the workset when objective checks pass.

Start by reading:
- AGENTS.md.
- OPERATIONS.md sections Bead Loop, Verification, and Git Discipline.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md sections Closure Condition, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md W002 row.
- The closed outputs and commit history for oxforms-dwm.2 through oxforms-dwm.5.

Scope:
- Gather the final evidence for W002: Rust fixture command/output/hash, OxVba smoke command/output/hash, Windows visible smoke result or blocker, platform notes, and exact commands run.
- Add or update evidence docs under docs/ as appropriate for this repo stage. Keep evidence concise but reproducible.
- Update docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md and docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md to reflect final status, residual work, and any blocker/follow-up beads.
- Do a fresh-eyes review of the entire W002 implementation surface: docs, tests, command names, dependency policy, smoke-only wording, and bead graph.
- File any newly discovered out-of-scope work as beads before closing this bead.
- Close oxforms-dwm only if the workset closure condition is truly met.

Non-goals:
- Do not sneak in new renderer features. If evidence review discovers missing implementation, send it back to the relevant bead or create a focused follow-up.
design:
Design notes:
- This bead is the guardrail against optimistic closure. It should verify that W002 still proves exactly what it set out to prove: VBA-authored FillRect reaches PAL and renders, with headless evidence and Windows plumbing.
- If Windows visible smoke is not actually verified on Windows, do not hide that. Record the concrete blocker and create the follow-up bead required by the workset closure condition.
- Keep closure language precise: smoke implemented, not Forms runtime implemented.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Evidence docs link or quote the exact commands and artifacts for Rust headless, OxVba smoke, and Windows visible smoke or blocker.
- Workset docs and WORKSET_REGISTER status are accurate.
- br dep cycles reports no cycles and br ready --json is reviewed for expected next work.
- All relevant code checks from prior beads have been rerun or their latest successful outputs are cited; at minimum run git diff --check and br graph checks in this bead.
- Any out-of-scope findings are filed as beads before closure.
- oxforms-dwm epic is closed only if all closure conditions are actually met.
- Commit evidence/docs/bead state with this bead ID in the message.
notes:
Dependencies: blocked by oxforms-dwm.4 and oxforms-dwm.5. This bead closes the workset only after both smoke paths are proven or explicitly handled.

At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.
